slides.title: Section 1 Reflections
slides.notes:
§SECTION 1 REFLECTIONS

§HOW TO USE THIS SLIDE:

§1. Show the slide and read the two prompts aloud.
1 · Overview reflection: "Take one Key Result your group confirmed in Unit 3. What is it assuming about the world that has not yet been verified?"

2 · Bringing ABCV Together reflection: "Which of the four ABCV checkpoints is your organisation least likely to examine rigorously before launching a new strategic initiative? What does that pattern cost you?"

§2. Say what the reflection is for.
Point learners to the portal section that they will be required to complete with as much depth as possible.
The reflections build the learning portfolio they receive at the end of the programme.

Say: "You write this reflection on the portal after the teaching, with as much depth as you can."

§3. Set the standard.
Say: "For the first reflection, name one real Key Result of your group and one thing it assumes. For the second, name the checkpoint and one real cost."
Listen for: an assumption stated as a worry. Ask: "Written as a condition, is it true or false today?"

§4. Bridge to Section 2.
Say: "We have the four checkpoints. Section 2 asks why leaders so often fail to use them."

§ON THE PORTAL, AFTER THE TEACHING:
Participants write the two reflections in Section 1 of the participant file: under the overview, and under Bringing ABCV Together.

slides.title: Section 3 Reflections
slides.notes:
§SECTION 3 REFLECTIONS

§HOW TO USE THIS SLIDE:

§1. Show the slide and read the prompt aloud.
3.1 Reflection: "Having explored your role’s typical blind spot: what is one MBT condition in that checkpoint that your organisation is currently assuming without confirmation? What would it take to verify it?"

§2. Say what the reflection is for.
Point learners to the portal section that they will be required to complete with as much depth as possible.
The reflections build the learning portfolio they receive at the end of the programme.

Say: "You write this reflection on the portal after the teaching, with as much depth as you can."

§3. Set the standard.
Say: "Name the checkpoint of your role.
Write one condition your organisation is assuming, in a form that is either true or false.
Then say what evidence would verify it and who holds that evidence."
Listen for: a general concern where a condition is needed. Ask: "What exactly must remain true?"

§4. Bridge to Section 4.
Say: "We know the checkpoints and we know our blind spots. Section 4 applies both to your own Key Results."

§ON THE PORTAL, AFTER THE TEACHING:
Participants write the reflection in Section 3 of the participant file: 3.1 Reflection.

pictures.alt: Reflection 3.1: Having explored your role’s typical blind spot: what is one MBT condition in that checkpoint that your organisation is currently assuming without confirmation? What would it take to verify it?

slides.title: Section 5 Reflections
slides.after: Cause of Death · The Four Mines
slides.notes:
§SECTION 5 REFLECTIONS

§HOW TO USE THIS SLIDE:

§1. Show the slide and read the prompt aloud.
Closing Commitment: "What is one MBT condition your organisation is currently avoiding naming? Why? What will you do about it before your next strategic review?"

§2. Say what the reflection is for.
Point learners to the portal section that they will be required to complete with as much depth as possible.
The reflections build the learning portfolio they receive at the end of the programme.

Say: "You write this reflection on the portal after the teaching, with as much depth as you can."

§3. Set the standard.
Say: "Name one condition, in a form that is either true or false.
Say why it is being avoided.
Then name one action and the date of your next strategic review."

Deepen, say: "The instinct to manage the appearance of a known exposure, and leave the exposure itself unaddressed, turns a survivable warning into a failure.
A risk that has been named and then avoided chooses its own moment.
Treat a clear warning as a directive to act."
(Insight: Named and avoided. Source: Journal, 16 June 2026 — Professional Insights: Strategy)

§ON THE PORTAL, AFTER THE TEACHING:
Participants write the Closing Commitment at the end of Section 5 of the participant file.
